title: Local AI Agent (Human-in-the-Loop)
tagline: Desktop agent with a local LLM and mandatory human approval
problem: I wanted a real AI agent running 100% on my machine — no paid API, no data leaving the PC — without giving up safety: a local model must not be able to write files or run commands on its own.
targetUser: Myself (personal tool; the data scope explicitly excludes anything work-related).
myRole: Sole developer: desktop app, Rust backend, LLM integration.
process: Tauri 2 (Rust) + React + TypeScript desktop app, local LLM via Ollama. Built with real TDD on the Rust backend (sandbox, agenda and audit modules have test suites). The model answers with a "structured intent" (JSON proposing an action: write file, read, run command) that lands in an approval queue with a diff before anything executes.
keyDecisions: Non-negotiable human-in-the-loop: the model only proposes; every execution goes through Approve/Reject. No autonomous mode, hidden or otherwise.
Tauri over Electron: real declarative sandboxing — the frontend never touches filesystem/processes directly, only through exposed Rust commands.
File sandbox with canonicalize() + workspace prefix check (tested against .., absolute paths, new files).
Terminal sandbox limits documented honestly: cwd pinned to the workspace, but the real defense is manual approval of the exact command.
Append-only audit log (JSONL), tolerant to corrupted lines.
result: Working agent: chat with a local model, approval queue with diffs, sandboxed file/terminal execution, conversation history, personal checklist agenda and an action-reports view — all offline.
learned: Rust + Tauri for real (capabilities, tests, defensive parsing — local models sometimes wrap JSON in code fences and the parser must survive it). And an agent's safety architecture is a product decision, not a detail: proposing ≠ executing, and that line must live in the runtime, not in the prompt.
